newsitem.title: RUSSIA: RUSSIA MINFINS UP ON PAPER SHORTAGE, TREND UNCLEAR.
newsitem.headline: RUSSIA MINFINS UP ON PAPER SHORTAGE, TREND UNCLEAR.

text.p: Russian MinFin bonds edged up in thin trading on Tuesday on a severe paper shortage, but dealers said the market was at a cross-roads after the recent rally.
They gave mixed forecasts of the trend in the next few days.
"The market is up on a most terrible absence of paper," said a Moscow bank dealer. "There are 10 buyers for each sale."
He forecast a sliding market after the United States announces its July Producer Price Index on Wednesday.
"We are expecting that the index will be high and on the back of it paper will appear," he said. "At least for Moscow banks, it will be bloodshed."
He said Russian banks preferred to hold MinFins rather than diversifying their portfolios into other Bradies.
But the MinFin market, with a total volume of about $7 billion, was relatively illiquid and risky, he said.
The U.S. will issue the July consumer price index on Thursday.
MinFins, like other emerging market debt, move in line with U.S. Treasury bonds and so are sensitive to news affecting U.S. interest rates.
Another dealer, estimating Tuesday's rise in prices at about 0.1 basis points, said operators were unsure what to do.
"People are disconcerted -- it is too high to buy, but the market is too firm for selling, they cannot break support levels," he said.
He said the support level for tranche 3 was 91.70, for the fourth tranche 70.5, for the fifth tranche 53.0, for the sixth tranche 59.0 and for the seventh tranche 47.0.
